title: AUTHORITATIVE PRODUCT REFERENCE differs from INTENDED SCIENTIFIC REFERENCE

verification.method: the reference pixel is identically zero across every date
verification.conclusion: the product is referenced to the authoritative pixel; the intended pixel is not the reference

measured_offset.sign_convention: the authoritative product reads the intended reference pixel at this velocity, so re-basing adds it to every pixel to convert to the intended zero level

ERA5.note: The reference mismatch contributes a constant term. Aligning shifts the median by the offset and leaves the RMS essentially unchanged, so no branch verdict is affected.

ERA5+DEM.note: The reference mismatch contributes a constant term. Aligning shifts the median by the offset and leaves the RMS essentially unchanged, so no branch verdict is affected.

effect_on_phase1_results.reason: InSAR velocities are defined relative to a reference pixel. Changing the reference adds one constant to every pixel, so every difference between two pixels is invariant.

reporting_requirement: Every subsequent report must label velocity values as relative to either the AUTHORITATIVE PRODUCT REFERENCE (1384,1451) or the INTENDED SCIENTIFIC REFERENCE (1378,1426). The two must not be mixed silently. Phase I values are relative to the authoritative product reference.
remediation: Fix at the next product revision by setting mintpy.reference.yx explicitly in EVERY branch config. `config/mintpy_era5.txt` and `config/mintpy_dem_residual.txt` already set it; `config/mintpy_baseline_raw.txt` does not.
